newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: At least eight killed by violent Pakistan quake.
newsitem.headline: At least eight killed by violent Pakistan quake.

text.p: A violent earthquake jolted Pakistan's southwestern province of Baluchistan early on Friday, killing at least eight people and injuring many others, residents and officials said.
An official at a seismic centre in the northwestern town of Peshawar described the earthquake as "violent" but could not immediately give its strength on the international Richter scale.
He said the quake's strength could be more than 6.5, which can cause widespread damage.
At least three people were killed and 20 injured in Quetta, the provincial capital, and five at Sibi in the southeast of Quetta, doctors said.
The quake struck Quetta at 2:10 a.m. (2110 GMT Thursday) and continued shaking the city for half a minute. Mild tremors were being felt in the city even two hours after the first jolt.
Almost the entire city population woke up and came out of their homes in freezing cold, residents said.
Even hospital patients came of their wards with their beds.
"First there was a mild tremor, then it became very severe and it sounded as though a tractor was running outside," one resident said.
Islamic religious men went to mosques and called Azan, the Moslem call for prayers, as is usually done in the event of calamity. Many people fired automatic weapons in the air to wake up people.
The region is prone to earthquakes. Quetta waa destroyed by an earthquake on May 31, 1935, which measured 7.5 on the Richter scale and killed 30,000 people.
